raw_affiliation_string: Androula Michael is a contemporary art historian and professor at the University of Picardie Jules Verne (Amiens, France), and director of the Centre for Research in Art and Aesthetics (CRAE, UR 4291, Université de Picardie Jules Verne). She is also an associate researcher at the Center for International Studies (CERI), Sciences Po Paris. She co-directs the research program Doctorate Picasso (Museu Picasso de Barcelona, Autonomous University of Barcelona, and University of Picardie Jules Verne). As part of her research residency at the Musée national Picasso-Paris and at CERI, she contributes to the project Réceptions critiques de Picasso en Amérique latine. In collaboration with Barthélémy Toguo, she also leads the project Retours à l’Afrique : depuis la perspective des Amériques. Together with Anne-Claire Faucquez, she works on the representation of colonial slavery in the arts and museums in the United States. Her current research focuses on the work of Picasso, the cross-critical reception of Pablo Picasso and Marcel Duchamp, contemporary art in de/post/colonial contexts, silences and the erasure of memory, as well as the representation of colonial slavery in the arts and museums. A member of AICA, she is also an independent curator. Among other publications, she is the author of the exhibition catalogues Returns to Africa.
